- **Christian Parker** — The Cowboys’ defensive overhaul is essentially complete after the draft, with a new 3-4 base under Parker driving major turnover in the starting lineup. Dallas is still open to adding help — it met with Adoree’ Jackson last week — but the heavy lifting is done. That matters because the scheme change could keep creating role churn on defense even if the front office is mostly finished shopping. [4]

- **Ryan Flournoy** — Flournoy has emerged as the clear frontrunner for Dallas’ WR3 job behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The note specifically says he has quietly forced his way into the offensive picture with grit and willingness to do whatever helps the team. For fantasy, he’s the name to watch in a secondary receiving role if the pecking order holds. [6]

- **Phil Mafah** — Mafah is part of a Cowboys running back group with “a lot of intrigue,” and the backup spots are described as wide open. Dallas added him in the 2025 seventh round after waiting until Day 3 to address RB, then later pairing him with Jaydon Blue. His physical style gives him a different path than Blue’s speed, so the camp battle should matter for the depth chart. [7]

- **Donovan Ezeiruaku** — Ezeiruaku is being framed as the best bet among Dallas’ second-year players to make a big leap in 2026. Even with frequent rotation as a rookie, he generated pressure in all but two games and finished with two sacks and a 12.6% pass-rush win rate. That points to real breakout upside if his role expands. [8]

- **Avieon Terrell** — The rookie is expected to have a real path to a role, but the exact fit is still unsettled: the article says it’s not clear whether he opens as a starter inside, starter outside, or a reserve. If he’s going to line up with A.J. Terrell Jr., he likely has to beat out Mike Hughes or Billy Bowman Jr., and Bowman is coming back from an Achilles injury that cost him the back half of his rookie year. That makes the cornerback battle one of the more interesting early depth-chart fights to watch. [5]

- **Kendal Daniels** — Atlanta drafted Daniels in the fourth round to capitalize on his versatility, and the team wants to develop him as a potential starter, possibly even as a replacement for Kaden Elliss after Elliss left in free agency to New Orleans. Daniels lined up at linebacker, nickel corner, and even edge rusher at Oklahoma, so his role could expand in multiple ways if the staff leans into that hybrid usage. His immediate value may be tied to how quickly the Falcons can turn that flexibility into a defined NFL job. [8]

- **Bijan Robinson** — Robinson is being framed as Atlanta’s biggest reason for optimism entering 2026, with the note highlighting that he drove the late-season surge. He finished with 2,298 yards from scrimmage, including three games over 150 yards from scrimmage in the final four, and he impacted games as both a runner and receiver. That kind of workload keeps him central to the offense and makes him the clearest fantasy anchor on the roster. [7]

- **Zane Gonzalez** — Gonzalez was one of Atlanta’s standout individual performers, going 4-for-4 on field goals and 1-for-1 on extra points in the season finale against New Orleans. He accounted for 13 of the Falcons’ 19 points, including two fourth-quarter makes that helped close out the Saints. The result is useful context for a position that can be volatile, even if the broader roster questions are elsewhere. [3]
